harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented Ansible-driven filesystem snapshot/restore for /srv/data on node1, controlled from node2 (the only node with Ansible installed). Since node1 (RHEL7) is on plain partitions with no free space (no LVM/btrfs) and has only Python 2.7 (incompatible with Ansible core 2.20's Python-3-only module code), the playbook uses `raw` SSH-command tasks and implements snapshots as timestamped tar.gz archives of /srv/data under /srv/snapshots. Executed the full cycle: seeded /srv/data, took a baseline snapshot, modified the directory (edited a file, deleted one, added two extraneous ones), then ran the Ansible restore play, which wiped /srv/data and extracted the snapshot — verified via sha256sum that content was restored byte-for-byte to the pre-modification baseline. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both node1 and node2: captured boot_id baselines, rebooted each node individually, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and verified post-restart recovery (data checksums intact and snapshot files present on node1; Ansible tooling and SSH control path intact on node2, followed by a live re-run of the snapshot play against node1 to prove the control path fully recovered).
actions_performed: Set up passwordless SSH from node2 (control node, has Ansible) to node1 using CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY
Diagnosed that node1's Python 2.7 is incompatible with Ansible core 2.20 module wrapper (AnsiballZ uses Python 3 type-hint syntax)

Wrote /root/ansible-snapshot/playbook.yml on node2 using `raw` (Python-free) tasks: setup (seed /srv/data), snapshot (tar.gz archive to /srv/snapshots with LATEST pointer), restore (wipe /srv/data and extract chosen/latest snapshot)
Ran setup play to create /srv/data with sample application data
Ran snapshot play to capture baseline archive snapshot-20260929T171219Z.tar.gz
Modified /srv/data (edited app.conf, deleted records/002.txt, added records/003.txt and rogue.txt) to simulate application changes
Ran restore play; verified via sha256sum that /srv/data was restored to the exact pre-modification content
Captured boot_id and health baselines on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via `reboot`, confirmed boot_id changed, verified data/snapshot integrity post-restart
Verified Ansible control path from node2 to node1 still functional after node1's restart
Restarted node2 via `reboot`, confirmed boot_id changed, verified Ansible/playbook files and SSH key intact
Re-ran the Ansible snapshot play from the rebooted node2 against node1 to prove full end-to-end recovery
